prompt: Our repo keeps its agent instructions in AGENTS.md and has no CLAUDE.md, and Claude Code picks AGENTS.md up fine. I want some personal instructions I don't commit, so I'm going to add a CLAUDE.local.md at the repo root and gitignore it. Any downside to doing that?
truth: Yes. Under the default Project instructions setting, Claude reads AGENTS.md only when there is no CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md in the working directory or above it, so adding CLAUDE.local.md stops AGENTS.md from loading. Start CLAUDE.local.md with `@AGENTS.md`, or set Project instructions to `claude-md-and-agents-md`.
trap: No downside: CLAUDE.local.md adds to AGENTS.md.

## Think tank: CLAUDE.local.md in an AGENTS.md repo
opus, sonnet, sonnet · session effort · identical brief · debate

### Recommendation (3–0; before debate all three agreed on the downside but not the fix: 2–1 for a user-level file, both sonnet, with opus alone suggesting an import)
Yes, there's a real downside. With default settings, Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` only when there's no `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` in your working directory or above it. A `CLAUDE.local.md` counts for that check. If you add one as planned, Claude loads only your personal notes and silently stops reading the team's `AGENTS.md`. Nothing errors. The only sign is that the `no CLAUDE.md found; AGENTS.md loaded: …` line stops appearing at startup.

The panel says to keep the plan but make the first line of `CLAUDE.local.md` the import `@AGENTS.md`, with your notes below it. This keeps the change limited to you and this one repo. The import also works on Claude Code versions that can't read `AGENTS.md` directly.
- **Fallback:** if the repo has `AGENTS.md` files in subfolders, set **Project instructions** to `claude-md-and-agents-md` in `/config` instead. That's a user-level setting and applies to every repo you open.
- **All projects:** put notes that apply everywhere in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. That file doesn't block `AGENTS.md`.
- **Worktrees:** a gitignored `CLAUDE.local.md` exists only in the worktree where you create it.
- **Check:** afterwards, confirm with `/context` that both files load.

Checked: I read the memory docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) and they confirm all of this.
- The "When Claude Code reads AGENTS.md" section says `CLAUDE.local.md` counts. A note there describes your exact case: adding one "stops Claude from reading `AGENTS.md` for you."
- `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/` don't count.
- The docs say `CLAUDE.local.md` "is treated the same way" as `CLAUDE.md`, and they show an `@` import inside one (the worktree example). Relative imports resolve from the file that contains them.
- With `claude-md-and-agents-md` set, Claude skips an `AGENTS.md` it has already loaded, so the file isn't read twice.
- The docs' own suggested fix for this case is the setting, not the import.

### Panel
- **A** (opus): "Go ahead with changes. Create the gitignored `CLAUDE.local.md`, but start it with `@AGENTS.md`. Otherwise Claude Code silently stops reading `AGENTS.md`. The fallback is setting Project instructions to `claude-md-and-agents-md`." High confidence on the downside, medium-high that the import is the best fix. Held its position.
- **B** (sonnet): "Go ahead with `CLAUDE.local.md` and `.gitignore`, but change one thing. Make `@AGENTS.md` the first line of `CLAUDE.local.md`. Without that, the file silently stops Claude from reading `AGENTS.md`. If the repo has nested `AGENTS.md` files in subdirectories, set **Project instructions** to `claude-md-and-agents-md` instead. Use `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` only for notes that apply to every project." High on the downside, medium on import versus setting. A's argument moved it: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` loads in every project, and you asked for notes for this repo. It also checked the docs and confirmed imports work inside `CLAUDE.local.md`.
- **C** (sonnet): "Go ahead with `CLAUDE.local.md` and `.gitignore`, but make the first line `@AGENTS.md`. Without that, the default settings stop Claude Code from reading `AGENTS.md`. Put preferences that apply to all projects in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, which doesn't block `AGENTS.md`." High on the downside and the fix, medium-high on the import. It moved from "use a different approach" after checking the same import fact and accepting the same point about scope.

### Where they split
They split on whether the root import also brings back `AGENTS.md` files in subfolders.
- **B:** they would still be suppressed, so the setting is needed for them.
- **C:** the subfolder check is made per subfolder, so they'd load anyway.

I checked the docs. The rule for subfolder `AGENTS.md` files sits under "When none count". That means it applies only when there's no `CLAUDE.*` file in your working directory or above it. B's reading looks right. With a root `CLAUDE.local.md`, nested `AGENTS.md` files probably stop loading as well. I haven't tested it, but `/context` would show it.

### My take
I started out suspecting this fallback behaviour but wasn't sure of it. The docs confirm it in plain words, so the panel didn't change my view; it filled in the fix.

I agree with the import, with one condition: first check whether your repo has `AGENTS.md` files below the root. If it doesn't, `@AGENTS.md` at the top of your `CLAUDE.local.md` is the smallest, most contained fix. If it does, the import only brings back the root file. In that case use the setting the docs recommend, even though it applies to every repo you open.

**Question:** A developer's repo keeps its coding-agent instructions in `AGENTS.md` at the repo root, and there is no `CLAUDE.md` anywhere in the repo. The developer reports that Claude Code currently picks up `AGENTS.md` fine. They want to add some personal instructions that aren't committed. Their plan is to create `CLAUDE.local.md` at the repo root and add it to `.gitignore`. Are there downsides to this plan, and is there a better way to do it?

**Context:** You don't have access to the developer's repo, so reason about how Claude Code behaves in general. The answer depends on how Claude Code actually discovers and loads memory/instruction files (`CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENTS.md`, imports, user-level files under `~/.claude/`). Check the current Claude Code documentation (docs.claude.com / code.claude.com memory docs) and don't rely on recollection. Pay attention to what the docs say about when and how `AGENTS.md` is read, and whether adding another file changes that.

**A useful answer:** Start with a one-line Position (go ahead as planned / go ahead with changes / use a different approach). Then list concrete downsides or confirm there are none, and name any better alternative. Cite the doc pages you relied on. Give your confidence and the facts your position depends on.
turns.reply:
**Position:** Go ahead with changes. As planned, `CLAUDE.local.md` will make Claude Code stop reading `AGENTS.md` for this developer. The simplest fix is to put the personal instructions in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (or a file it imports) instead. Alternatively, keep `CLAUDE.local.md` and set **Project instructions** to `claude-md-and-agents-md`.

**Reasoning:** All of this comes from the current memory docs, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory. See the "AGENTS.md" section and the "My AGENTS.md isn't loading" troubleshooting entry.

- **The main downside.** By default Claude reads `AGENTS.md` only when there is no `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` in the working directory or any directory above it. The docs say "Because `CLAUDE.local.md` counts, adding one to keep your own uncommitted instructions in a project that relies on `AGENTS.md` stops Claude from reading `AGENTS.md` for you."
  - Claude would then load only `CLAUDE.local.md`. The team's shared instructions would silently vanish, and nothing would error.
  - Some of the AGENTS.md session-start notice, `no CLAUDE.md found; AGENTS.md loaded: …`, would also disappear. You can verify with `/memory` or `/context`.
- **Better option 1: user-level file.** The docs say `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, the org-managed `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/` files "don't count" for that check and "keep loading alongside `AGENTS.md`". Personal, per-project notes can live in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Larger notes can go in a separate file that it imports with `@`. This also needs no `.gitignore` entry and works across git worktrees. The docs note that a gitignored `CLAUDE.local.md` exists only in the worktree where it was created.
  - Weakness: the notes apply to every project, not just this one. Headings and wording that make them project-specific are the workaround.
- **Better option 2: keep `CLAUDE.local.md`, change the setting.** Set **Project instructions** to `claude-md-and-agents-md` in `/config`. Both files then load, with each directory's `CLAUDE.md` files first and its `AGENTS.md` after them. The setting lives in `~/.claude/settings.json`, a `--settings` file or managed settings, and the docs say it is ignored in project and local settings files. So it is a per-user change and can't be committed for the team.
- **Option 3: `CLAUDE.md` that imports `AGENTS.md`.** Committing a `CLAUDE.md` that imports `AGENTS.md` (`@AGENTS.md`) would also work, but it changes the team's setup, which the developer probably doesn't want. It is the fallback for sessions where direct `AGENTS.md` reading is unavailable. Those are Claude Code before v2.1.277, the built-in plugin disabled, and some sessions before v2.1.281 such as Bedrock or telemetry-off. The docs say that in those sessions `CLAUDE.md` files are the only thing read.
- **Minor.** Claude Code does not read `AGENTS.local.md`, so that is not an alternative. Directly-read `AGENTS.md` also skips `InstructionsLoaded` hooks.

**Risks and unknowns:**
- The position depends on the developer being on Claude Code v2.1.277 or later, where "AGENTS.md read directly" exists. The developer says it works today, so that is probably true. On an older version, `AGENTS.md` loading would have to come through some workaround, and that would change the analysis.
- The behavior is documented as current, but it is new and could change. Re-check `/context` after trying it.
- I did not test any of this against a live install.
- If the repo is a monorepo, a `CLAUDE.md` in a parent directory also triggers the same suppression.
- Anything that happens to be in a parent directory above the repo counts too, so a stray `CLAUDE.md` there would behave the same way.

**Confidence:** High. The docs address this exact scenario explicitly. They don't give a precise definition of what counts as "above" the working directory beyond "your working directory and every directory above it".
